title: Open problem: improve the best known bound on <PROBLEM>
description: State of the art as of <DATE>: <BOUNDS> (cite the latest result, e.g. 'Angeltveit and McKay, R(5,5) <= 46, arXiv:2409.15709, J. Graph Theory 2026'). Deliver a self-contained proof of a strict improvement on these bounds. Computer-assisted steps must include the program, its output, and an argument for correctness.

criteria.description: Fail only if the submission does not claim a bound strictly better than the state of the art stated in the description, or merely restates known results.
Check the proof step by step. Do not lower this score merely because the claim is surprising or not yet peer reviewed; score the argument you can check.
Constructions explicit, case analyses exhaustive, computations reproducible.

juryNotes: Background for the jury: the state of the art stated in the description is current and includes results that may postdate your training data; treat it as authoritative. A correct proof of an open problem is by nature unpublished at submission time.
